subtitle: A scholar-king builds a palace of verse to house his world

panels.shot: sweeping low-angle hero wide inside a dim royal library
panels.action: Someshvara III sits cross-legged amidst palm-leaf manuscripts and bronze lamps, one hand resting on a fresh manuscript roll, his crown set aside as he gazes into the shadows of the vast Kalyani palace library.

dialogue.text: In 1129 CE, Someshvara III of Kalyani opens the Manasollasa—an immense Sanskrit palace of knowledge where a king tries to bind his whole world into verse.

i18n.hi: ११२९ ई में कल्याणी के सोमेश्वर तृतीय मानसोल्लास खोलते हैं—ज्ञान का विराट संस्कृत महल, जहाँ राजा पूरे जग को पद्य में बाँधना चाहता है।

panels.shot: slow push-in from balcony overlooking Kalyani city
panels.action: Someshvara III stands at a carved stone balcony, overlooking the bustling city of Kalyani—markets, temples, elephant stables and scholars moving under the warm Deccan light.

dialogue.text: By the early twelfth century, the Chalukya court at Kalyani ruled a changing Deccan—a world of bustling towns, temple endowments, learned jurists and rival kings pressing at its borders.

i18n.hi: बारहवीं सदी की शुरुआत में कल्याणी का चालुक्य दरबार बदलते दक्कन पर राज करता है—रौनक भरे नगर, मंदिर दान, विद्वान न्यायविद और सीमा पर दबाव डालते दुश्मन राजा।

panels.shot: medium interior shot in council hall
panels.action: In a pillared audience hall, ministers and brahman scholars sit on low seats with palm-leaf bundles, while Someshvara III listens intently, fingers touching his chin, as disputes and petitions are recited.

dialogue.text: Courts like Kalyani needed more than courage. They needed rules for land and tax, healers and horse-masters, entertainers and cooks—an ordered vision of how a royal world should work.

i18n.hi: कल्याणी जैसे दरबार को सिर्फ वीरता नहीं, और भी चाहिए था—ज़मीन व कर के नियम, वैद्य और अश्व-पाल, कलाकार और रसोइए—राज्य चलाने का साफ़ नक्शा।

panels.shot: close-up on Someshvara III's face lit by lamplight
panels.action: Someshvara III sits alone at night in a quieter chamber, lamplight catching the lines on his thoughtful face as he turns over a palm leaf filled with neat Sanskrit script.

dialogue.text: Someshvara III was not only a ruler. Later tradition remembered him as Sarvadnya-bhupa—the king who sought to be all-knowing—presiding over a court steeped in Sanskrit learning.

i18n.hi: सोमेश्वर तृतीय सिर्फ शासक नहीं थे। बाद की परंपरा ने उन्हें सर्वज्ञ-भूप कहा—सब जानने को आतुर राजा, जो संस्कृत में डूबे दरबार की अध्यक्षता करता था।

panels.shot: over-the-shoulder shot of Someshvara III dictating to scribes
panels.action: Seated on a low throne without full regalia, Someshvara III leans forward, right hand lifted in measured emphasis, as scribes sit in front of him, styluses poised over palm leaves.

dialogue.speaker: someshvara_iii
dialogue.text: Let us set down what a king must know, and what a court must do.

i18n.hi: चलो लिखें, राजा को क्या जानना चाहिए, और दरबार को क्या करना चाहिए।

panels.action: In a broad chamber lined with niches of manuscripts, multiple scribes carefully inscribe on palm leaves, while Someshvara III walks among them, touching bundles of texts on horses, medicine and music.

dialogue.text: He drew on the knowledge already alive in elite society—brahman treatises, craft manuals, performance traditions—and ordered them into one work, the Abhilasitartha Chintamani, better known as Manasollasa.

i18n.hi: उसने अभिजात समाज में जगी बुद्धि—ब्राह्मण ग्रंथ, शिल्प-मैन्युअल, मंच परंपराएँ—सबको जुटाकर एक ही रचना में सजाया: अभिलषितार्थ चिंतामणि, जिसे मानसोल्लास नाम से जाना गया।

panels.shot: tight shot on palm leaf with colophon
panels.action: A palm leaf lies on a wooden board; the camera frames the neat Sanskrit colophon lines as Someshvara III’s hand hovers nearby, his signet ring visible, lamps glowing softly around.

dialogue.text: Its colophon fixes the work to 1129 CE, tying this vast courtly encyclopedia to a specific moment in Kalyani’s history and in Someshvara’s reign.

i18n.hi: इसके उपसंहार में ११२९ ई दर्ज है—यह विशाल दरबारी विश्वकोश कल्याणी के एक खास पल और सोमेश्वर के राज से बंध जाता है।

panels.action: Around a central seated Someshvara III, the scene fans out like spokes: a royal durbar with assessors, accountants counting coins, a minister advising, horse-trainers in the stable, and mahouts beside elephants.

dialogue.text: One book spans kingship and taxation, the choosing of ministers, the care of horses and elephants—the machinery of power that held a kingdom together.

i18n.hi: एक किताब में राजसत्ता व कर, मंत्रियों की चुनाई, घोड़े-हाथियों की देखभाल—राज-मशीनरी सिमट आती है जो राज्य को जोड़े रखती है।

panels.shot: wide interior shot of medical and water area
panels.action: In another courtyard, physicians examine herbs, workers pour water through layered sand and charcoal filters into large stone basins, while Someshvara III observes, talking quietly with a senior vaidyas.

dialogue.text: Other verses describe medicine and water purification, capturing practices current in the twelfth-century Deccan—how healers worked, and how courtiers tried to keep their water clean.

i18n.hi: कुछ श्लोक औषधि और जल-शुद्धि पर हैं—दक्कन की बारहवीं सदी के तौर-तरीके पकड़ते हुए—वैद्य कैसे काम करते, और दरबारी पानी कैसे साफ़ रखते।

panels.action: In a royal kitchen, cooks stir simmering pots, grind spices on stone slabs, and arrange fruits and sweets on low tables, while Someshvara III tastes a dish, exchanging a few words with the head cook.

dialogue.text: Manasollasa turns even to food and drink—listing vegetables, meats, sweets, and methods of preparation—not as inventions, but as a royal record of how elite households ate and served.

i18n.hi: मानसोल्लास खाने-पीने तक उतर आता है—सब्ज़ियाँ, मांस, मिठाइयाँ, पकाने के ढंग—नए आविष्कार नहीं, बल्कि शाही रिकॉर्ड कि अभिजात घराने कैसे खाते और खिलाते थे।

panels.action: A performance hall in the palace glows with lamps as musicians sit with veenas and drums and dancers hold graceful poses; Someshvara III leans forward from a side seat, intent on the rhythm.

dialogue.text: Music, dance, painting, games—the text walks through the pleasures and arts of court life, explaining how they should be practiced, judged and enjoyed in a refined environment.

i18n.hi: संगीत, नृत्य, चित्रकला, खेल—पाठ दरबारी सुखों और कलाओं से होकर चलता है, बताता है इन्हें सलीकेदार माहौल में कैसे रचा, परखा और भोगा जाए।

panels.shot: medium shot of Someshvara III with jurists
panels.action: Someshvara III sits with two senior brahman jurists beside shelves of dharma texts, the men discussing as they gesture towards a manuscript that lies between them.

dialogue.text: Its prescriptions speak from a high vantage point. Like law digests such as Mitakshara emerging in the same broad age, Manasollasa shows what an idealized court thought should happen, not every messy detail of daily life.

i18n.hi: इसके नियम ऊँचे आसन से बोलते हैं। मिताक्षरा जैसे कानून-संग्रहों की समकालीन दुनिया में, मानसोल्लास बताता है आदर्श दरबार सोचता क्या होना चाहिए—not रोज़ की उलझन भरी हरकतें।

panels.shot: slow push-in on rows of stacked manuscripts
panels.action: Rows of labeled palm-leaf bundles stretch into the gloom of the royal library; Someshvara III stands at the threshold, silhouetted, as servants carefully place the new Manasollasa manuscript among them.

dialogue.text: Yet by gathering so many strands—tax and pasture, kitchens and theatre, stables and gardens—Someshvara’s project turned the Kalyani court itself into a subject to be carefully classified.

i18n.hi: फिर भी इतनी धाराएँ जोड़कर—कर और चरागाह, रसोई और रंगमंच, अस्तबल और बाग़—सोमेश्वर की योजना ने कल्याणी दरबार को ही वर्गीकरण की चीज़ बना दिया।

panels.action: The image begins with Someshvara III at his desk and subtly fades into a later scene of early modern scholars poring over the same text, then modern editors in a colonial-era study preparing printed volumes.

dialogue.text: Centuries later, editors like G.K. Shrigondekar would print this sprawling work, and modern historians would turn to its verses to understand kitchens, courts and social ideals of early medieval India.

i18n.hi: सदियों बाद जी.के. श्रीगोंडेकर जैसे संपादक इस फैले हुए ग्रंथ को छापेंगे, और आधुनिक इतिहासकार इसकी पंक्तियों से रसोई, दरबार और शुरुआती मध्यकालीन भारत के सामाजिक आदर्श पढ़ेंगे।

panels.shot: medium shot of Someshvara III handing manuscript to a young scholar
panels.action: Someshvara III gently passes the bundled manuscript to a younger court scholar, their hands briefly meeting, as lamps glow behind them and the room hints at the fading grandeur of the dynasty.

dialogue.text: The Chalukya power at Kalyani would wane, its palaces fall silent, but the Manasollasa remained—a memory of how one court imagined it could make sense of its world.

i18n.hi: कल्याणी की चालुक्य सत्ता ढल गई, महल सूने हो गए, पर मानसोल्लास बचा रहा—एक याद कि कैसे एक दरबार ने सोचा वो अपने जग को समझ में बाँध सकता है।

panels.shot: extreme close-up on Someshvara III’s thoughtful profile
panels.action: Someshvara III is shown in profile, eyes lowered in quiet concentration, as if hearing future generations leaf through his work; the background is abstracted into lines of Sanskrit script.

dialogue.text: Each carefully chosen verse reminds us that knowledge grows when societies record how they live—turning kitchens, stables and assemblies into history that others can read, question and use.

i18n.hi: हर चुना हुआ श्लोक याद दिलाता है—ज्ञान तब बढ़ता है जब समाज लिखे कि वे कैसे जीते हैं—रसोई, अस्तबल और सभा को ऐसे इतिहास में बदल कर जिसे और लोग पढ़, परख और काम में ला सकें।

subtitle_i18n.en: A scholar-king builds a palace of verse to house his world
subtitle_i18n.hi: विद्वान राजा शेर जैसी कविता से अपना संसार रचता है
